where: Section 3, 'Reading a system by its level'
problem: The decision procedure gives a wrong answer for the two lower levels. Its second question is 'Ask whether processes share the host kernel. If yes, the level is OS-level.' Every ordinary process on Linux shares the host kernel, so a plain JVM (application-level) and a WINE program (library-level) both match this test and get labelled OS-level, contradicting Section 2 and quiz Q2/Q3. The 'first match' rule therefore only works for hardware-level.
fix: Make the second question specific to isolation of user-space instances: 'Ask whether one host kernel runs several isolated user-space environments, each looking like a separate server, with no kernel image of its own (namespaces and cgroups). If yes, the level is OS-level.' Add one line: 'A JVM or a WINE program is an ordinary host process; it shares the kernel but is not an isolated user-space environment, so it does not match this test.'
